title: A `calc()` in a `resolution` media feature is a parse error
impact: Valid CSS rejected in strict mode (whole stylesheet fails). errorRecovery preserves the @media rule unchanged with a warning, so no output corruption. calc() inside resolution queries is rare in real stylesheets; no framework or project named, 0 reactions; part of the agent-style batch #1391-#1406. One commenter (ChrisX101010) says they have a fix on a fork branch but opened no PR.
summary: Resolution's parser only accepts a dimension token, so `(resolution: calc(2 * 1x))`, `(min-resolution: calc(1dppx + 1x))` and `(resolution >= calc(96dpi * 2))` error ('Unexpected token Colon' / 'Invalid media query' / 'Unexpected token Function'). Media Queries 4 gives resolution the value <resolution>, and css-values-4 allows math functions wherever their type is allowed; Chromium parses all three (serializes as calc(2dppx)). Since dpi/dpcm/dppx are all absolutely convertible, every calc over resolutions folds at parse time, so Resolution can resolve calc like Time does, without an AST change.
repro: 1406-repro.mjs. `@media (resolution: calc(2 * 1x)){.a{color:red}}` -> ERROR: Unexpected token Colon (local, 1.33.0, 1.32.0, 1.31.1). Controls: plain `(resolution: 2x)` and `(min-resolution: 192dpi)` OK; `image-set("a.png" calc(2 * 1x))` passes through unchanged.
evidence: repro.mjs on local master + 3 releases (all fail the same way). probe.mjs Chromium 153: matchMedia('(resolution: calc(2 * 1x))').media => '(resolution: calc(2dppx))', min-resolution sum and range form also parsed, '(resolution: calc(1 * 1x))' matches at DPR 1. Spec: mediaqueries-4 'Value: <<resolution>> | infinite'; css-values-4 Type Checking: 'It can be used anywhere a value of that type is allowed.' WPT has mq-calc-resolution.html. errorRecovery: rule preserved as written with warning 'Unexpected token Colon'.

fix.approach: Mirror src/values/time.rs: in Resolution::parse_with_range try Calc::<Resolution>::parse first and accept only a fully resolved Calc::Value (apply range); implement the Calc trait set for Resolution (Mul<f32>, AddInternal via dppx conversion, PartialOrd, Op/Map/Sign, TryFrom<Calc<Resolution>>, impl_try_from_angle!). Tests next to the existing resolution media query tests in src/lib.rs. No JS AST change.

draftReply:
Thanks, confirmed: Lightning CSS doesn't accept math functions in `<resolution>` values yet, so `(resolution: calc(2 * 1x))` is rejected even though it's valid per Media Queries 4 / CSS Values 4 and Chromium parses it. This reproduces on master and on 1.31-1.33. With `errorRecovery: true` the rule is kept as written with a warning, so that's a workaround for now. Since all resolution units are convertible, the fix should be able to resolve the calc() at build time (e.g. to `2x`), the same way `<time>` values are handled.
